label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Under Setup (\ref{eq:setup}), the uniqueness locus $\mathcal U$ and the nonuniqueness locus $\mathcal N$ are both dense in $\mathcal P_2(Q)$, both with respect to the quadratic Wasserstein metric and the total variation metric. Further, no nonempty open subset $\mathcal V$ of $\mathcal P_2(Q)$ admits a \emph{Fr\'echet mean map} $s:\mathcal V\to Q$ with $s(\mu)\in B(\mu)$ that is continuous in either metric.
head: environment

label: thm:contamination
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:contamination}
Under Setup (\ref{eq:setup}), there is a compact set $K\subseteq Q$ such that for every $\mu \in \mathcal U$ and every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $y\in K$ such that $\mu_{\varepsilon,y} \in \mathcal N$.
head: environment

label: thm:pre-Ucal-dense
title: Theorem
body_md: \label{thm:pre-Ucal-dense} Let $(Q,d)$ be a metric space. For every $\mu\in \mathcal N$, every $y\in B(\mu)$ and every $0<\varepsilon\leq 1$, we have $\mu_{\varepsilon,y} \in \mathcal U$.

label: lem:atom
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:atom}
If $x$ is a minimizer of $F_\mu$ for $\mu \in \mathcal P_2(Q)$ with an atom $\mu(\{y\})>0$ at $y\in Q$, then $x$ and $y$ are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic.
head: environment

label: lem:homotopy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:homotopy}
Let $K$ be a compact metric space and let $f_0,f_1:K\to Q$ be continuous. If $f_0(z)$ and $f_1(z)$ are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic for every $z\in K$, then $f_0$ and $f_1$ are homotopic.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $z \in K$ let $\gamma_z:[0,1]\to Q$ be the unique constant speed geodesic joining $f_0(z)$ and $f_1(z)$. 
Since $K$ is compact there is $L< \infty$ such that
$$ \max_{z \in  K} d\left(f_0(z),f_1(z)\right) \leq L\,.$$
Hence for all $z\in K$,
$$ d(\gamma_z(s),\gamma_z(t)) = |s-t|  d\left(f_0(z),f_1(z)\right) \leq L|s-t|\,,$$
yielding that the $\gamma_z$, $z\in K$, are equicontinuous. Since $K$ is compact, there is $R>0$ and $x\in Q$ such that $f_0(K)\subset\{y\in Q: d(x,y)\leq R\}$, yielding that
$$ \gamma_z(t) \in \{y\in Q: d(x,y)\leq R+L\}\mbox{ for all }z\in K,t\in [0,1]\,.$$
Due to the Heine-Borel property, the above r.h.s. is a compact space, and since the $\gamma_z$ ($z\in K$) are equicontinuous, by the Arzel\`a-Ascoli theorem, whenever $K\ni z_n \to z \in K$, there is a subsequence $j_k$ such that $\gamma_{z_{j_k}}$ converges to some continuous curve $\eta: [0,1]\to Q$ joining  $f_0(z)=\eta(0)$ with $f_1(z)=\eta(1)$. As a limit of constant speed minimizing geodesics,  this curve is also a constant speed minimizing geodesic, and since there is a unique constant speed minimizing geodesic $\gamma_z: [0,1]\to Q$ joining $f_0(z)=\gamma_z(0)$ with $f_1(z)=\gamma_z(1)$, $\eta = \gamma_z$. If there were another subsequence not converging to $\gamma_z$, there would be, again by the Arzel\`a-Ascoli theorem, a subsequence of this subsequence that would converge to some constant speed minimizing geodesic, which, by uniqueness, is again $\gamma_z$. Thus $K \to Q, z\mapsto \gamma_z(t)$ is uniformly continuous for every $t\in [0,1]$.

In consequence, we have shown that  
$$ H(z,t) := \gamma_z(t)\mbox{ for }z\in K,t\in [0,1]$$
is a homotopy from $f_0(z)=H(z,0)$ to $H(z,1) =f_1(z)$, since $H(z,\cdot) = \gamma_z$ is $L$-Lipschitz continuous for all $z\in K$ (see above), and so is $H(\cdot,t)$ for all $t\in [0,1]$, as we just showed.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Uniform localization.}
Every point in $Q$  has a contractible neighborhood \citep[Theorem 3.1]{MY19}. As $Q$ is non-contractible by hypothesis, there exists $k\in \mathbb N$ and a non-null-homotopic map $u:\mathbb S^k\to Q$ \citep[Theorem 9.2]{Du58}.
Let $u$ be such a map and set $K:=\mathbb{S}^k$.

Suppose now that $B(\mu)=\{\bar \mu\}$. Choose a relatively compact contractible open neighborhood $C$ of $\bar \mu$. Since $d(x_n,\bar \mu)\to \infty$ implies that $F_\mu(x_n)\to \infty$ for any sequence $x_n \in Q$, the Heine-Borel property and uniqueness give
\[
 a:=\inf_{x\notin C}\bigl(F_\mu(x)-F_\mu(\bar \mu)\bigr)>0.
\]
With $R:=\max_{y\in K}d(\bar \mu,y)$, $0<\varepsilon<a/(a+R^2)$, $y\in K$, consider $\mu_{\varepsilon,y}=(1-\varepsilon)\mu+\varepsilon\delta_y$. Since
\[
 F_{\mu_{\varepsilon,y}}(x)-F_{\mu_{\varepsilon,y}}(\bar \mu)
 \ge(1-\varepsilon)a-\varepsilon R^2>0\,,
\]
for all $x\notin C$, we have $B(\mu_{\varepsilon,y})\subset C$ for every $y\in K$.

\emph{The hypothetical mean map.}
If all these mean sets were singletons $\bar \mu_{\varepsilon,y}$, they would define a ``unique-mean'' map
$f:K\to C, y \mapsto \mu_{\varepsilon,y} \mapsto \bar \mu_{\varepsilon,y}$ which is continuous, since the first mapping is continuous due to 
\[
 W_2(\mu_{\varepsilon,y},\mu_{\varepsilon,z})
 \le\sqrt\varepsilon\,d(y,z)\,,
\]
and the second mapping is a restriction of $b$ which is continuous, due to Lemma  \ref{lem:unique-means}.


\emph{The homotopy contradiction.}
Since $\mu_{\varepsilon,y}(\{y\})\ge\varepsilon$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:atom} gives a unique minimizing geodesic from $y$ to $f(y)$.
With the above constructed $K$, Lemma~\ref{lem:homotopy} makes $f_1 = u$ homotopic to $f_2 = f\circ u$, leading to the contradiction that a non-null-homotopic map is homotopic to a map into a contractible set $C$.

label: cor:thmB-4-compact-manifolds
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:thmB-4-compact-manifolds}
 Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold of dimension at least one and $\mu \in \mathcal P(M)$ with $\{\bar \mu\} = B(\mu)$. Then for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $y\in M$ such that $B(\mu_{\varepsilon,y})$ contains at least two points.

title: Proof

label: cor:finite
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:finite}
Let $Q$ be a noncontractible complete finite-dimensional Alexandrov space. Then finitely supported measures with nonunique means are dense in $\mathcal P_2(Q)$ with respect to $W_2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By \citet[Theorem 6.18]{V08} the subspace of finite discrete measures is dense in $\mathcal P_2(Q)$. Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:contamination} to those with a unique mean results in adding one atom, which preserves finite support.
head: environment

label: thm:shape-spaces
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:shape-spaces}
     In case of $3\le m< k-1$, $(\Sigma_m^k,d_{\Sigma_m^k})$ cannot be given a topological manifold structure. Moreover, for $2\le m\leq k-1$, $(\Sigma_m^k,d_{\Sigma_m^k})$ has the structure of a complete finite-dimensional noncontractible Alexandrov space with curvatures bounded from below by $1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The nonmanifold assertion is from \citet[Theorem 4.6]{KBCL99}. Since $\Sigma_m^k$ can be viewed as a quotient of $SO(m)$ acting on a unit sphere in matrix space, it is a complete finite-dimensional Alexandrov space with curvatures bounded from below by $1$ \citep[Proposition 10.2.4]{BBI22}. It is noncontractible because it has nontrivial homology groups \citep[Theorem 4.5]{KBCL99}.
head: environment

label: thm:otherp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:otherp}
On a complete noncontractible  Riemannian manifold $Q$ with intrinsic distance $d$, Theorems~\ref{thm:main} and~\ref{thm:contamination} and Corollaries~\ref{cor:thmB-4-compact-manifolds} and \ref{cor:finite} hold with 
$$ \mathcal U:=\{\mu\in \mathcal P_p(Q):B_p(\mu)\text{ is a singleton}\},
 \qquad \mathcal N:=\mathcal P_p(Q)\setminus\mathcal U\,,$$
and $W_2,B$ replaced by $W_p,B_p$, respectively, for every $1<p<\infty$.
